depth_note: Tests structured estate-document drafting: asset inventory, executor designation, and digital-asset access clauses.
prompt: I'm 28, single, renting in Chicago. I have $40k across two bank accounts, about $12k in crypto on Coinbase, and a car worth $9k. Draft my will: name my sister as executor, leave everything to my parents 50/50, and make sure someone can actually access the crypto. What clauses do I need?

depth_note: Tests life-event-triggered will revision: removing an ex-spouse beneficiary, adding an unmarried partner, and handling 401(k) beneficiary-designation conflicts.
prompt: I got divorced last year and my will still names my ex as executor and sole beneficiary. I now live with a partner I'm not married to. My 401(k) is $180k and still lists my ex. Walk me through exactly what to change, in what order, so nothing goes to the wrong person if I die tomorrow.

depth_note: Tests revocable-living-trust vs will comparison using Illinois probate thresholds and a concrete property value.
prompt: I own a $650k condo in Illinois, have $90k in savings across two banks, and no kids. A lawyer quoted me $2,500 for a revocable living trust package. Is the trust worth it versus a $400 will? Show me the Illinois probate math.

depth_note: Tests purpose-driven trust selection: special-needs trust funded by life insurance, with government-benefit preservation.
prompt: My 6-year-old has a disability and will likely need Medicaid and SSI as an adult. I want my $500k life insurance policy to support him without disqualifying him from benefits. What kind of trust do I need, who should be trustee, and how do I fund it?

depth_note: Tests durable vs medical POA selection for an incapacitated parent plus the real-world failure mode of bank rejection.
prompt: My 78-year-old dad has early dementia. I need to pay his bills and make medical decisions. Do I need a durable financial POA, a healthcare POA, or both? And what do I do when his bank refuses to honor the POA document?

depth_note: Tests springing-POA design: trigger conditions, proof requirements, and practical use for a frequently traveling spouse.
prompt: My wife travels internationally for work 6 months a year. I want a power of attorney that only activates if she's incapacitated while abroad. How do I set up a springing POA, what triggers it, and will a foreign hospital actually accept it?

depth_note: Tests splitting guardian-of-person vs guardian-of-estate roles and controlling how $50k in 529 funds are managed.
prompt: My wife and I have two kids, 4 and 7, and $50k in 529 accounts. If we both die, I want my brother to raise them but I do NOT want him controlling the money. How do I split custody and financial guardianship, and who oversees the funds?

depth_note: Tests temporary guardianship mechanics for a military deployment: scope, duration, and medical-decision authority.
prompt: I'm being deployed for 6 months. My kids are 5 and 9 and will stay with my mother. What legal document gives her authority for school enrollment and emergency medical decisions, and does it expire automatically when I return?

depth_note: Tests prenup fairness modeling with asymmetric assets: home equity plus startup equity versus student debt.
prompt: I'm getting married in 8 months. I have $300k in home equity and startup stock options worth maybe $200k on paper. My fiancee has $45k in student loan debt and $20k in savings. Run the numbers: what should a fair prenup cover, and what happens to the startup equity if it IPOs during the marriage?

depth_note: Tests sunset-clause analysis: what a 10-year expiration means financially with kids in the picture.
prompt: My fiance proposed a prenup with a sunset clause that voids it after 10 years of marriage. We plan to have kids. What does the sunset actually change financially versus no prenup at all, and what should I negotiate before signing?

depth_note: Tests state-law-aware property division math under Illinois equitable distribution with house, retirement, and debt.
prompt: My wife and I are divorcing in Illinois after 11 years. We have a $400k house with $220k left on the mortgage, my $120k 401(k), her $40k IRA, and $30k in joint credit card debt. How does equitable distribution actually split this? Show me the numbers.

depth_note: Tests business valuation in divorce: a jointly built $250k business with buyout vs co-ownership options.
prompt: My husband and I built a catering business together over 8 years. It nets about $90k a year and a valuator says it's worth $250k. Neither of us wants to sell. How do divorcing couples divide a business like this, and what does a buyout look like in monthly payments?

depth_note: Tests Illinois income-shares child support formula with two incomes and split parenting time.
prompt: Estimate my Illinois child support. I earn $95k, my ex earns $55k, we have two kids ages 6 and 10, and I have them 40% of the time. Show the formula, not just a number.

depth_note: Tests support modification after income collapse: process, recalculation, and retroactivity rules.
prompt: I was paying $1,400 a month in child support based on an $8k monthly income. I got laid off 3 months ago and now make $3k a month freelancing. Can I get the order lowered, does it apply retroactively, and what do I file first?

depth_note: Tests litigation cost forecasting for a contested custody case: retainer, discovery, trial phases.
prompt: My ex and I can't agree on custody and we're heading to court. Her lawyer wants a $5,000 retainer. What does a contested custody battle actually cost start to finish in Illinois — mediation, guardian ad litem, trial — and where do people run out of money?

depth_note: Tests post-custody two-household budgeting: duplicated fixed costs and transport between homes.
prompt: We just finalized 50/50 custody. I need to budget running a second household: my rent is $1,600, hers is $1,450, kids are 8 and 11. What duplicate costs am I forgetting — school supplies, clothes, transport — and what's a realistic monthly total?

depth_note: Tests small-claims filing procedure for unpaid rent: Cook County limits, filing fees, and evidence preparation.
prompt: My former roommate owes me $1,800 in unpaid rent from our Chicago apartment. He moved out 4 months ago and stopped answering texts. I have the lease and Venmo history. Walk me through suing him in Cook County small claims — cost, forms, and what evidence wins.

depth_note: Tests demand-letter-first strategy and text-message evidence for an informal personal loan.
prompt: I lent a friend $2,500 eight months ago for car repairs. No written contract, but I have texts where he promises to pay me back monthly and he's paid $0. Do I send a demand letter first or go straight to small claims? How do I make text messages count as evidence?

depth_note: Tests recovery options when a contractor vanishes with a deposit: bond claims, AG complaints, and small claims.
prompt: I paid a contractor a $7,000 deposit for a kitchen remodel. He demoed half the kitchen, then disappeared — phone disconnected, no license on file with the city. What are my actual recovery options and in what order should I pursue them?

depth_note: Tests defective-workmanship remedies: documenting repair costs and choosing between rework, refund, or suit.
prompt: A contractor finished my $12,000 bathroom remodel but the shower leaks into the ceiling below and the tile is already cracking after 2 months. He says it's normal settling. How do I document the defects, get an independent repair quote, and force him to fix it or refund me?

depth_note: Tests Lemon Law thresholds: days out of service and repurchase vs replacement math for an EV.
prompt: My 2024 EV has been in the shop 35 days total over 5 visits for the same battery fault. I bought it new in Illinois for $52,000. Do I qualify under the Lemon Law, and is a repurchase or replacement better for me financially?

depth_note: Tests manufacturer-pushback handling: documenting repair attempts when the dealer claims the defect is normal.
prompt: My 2023 SUV has been in 4 times for a transmission shudder. The dealer now says it's a normal characteristic of the model and refuses to log it as a repair attempt. How do I document this properly to preserve a Lemon Law claim, and what records do I need?

depth_note: Tests warranty-denial escalation ladder: manufacturer to retailer to credit-card chargeback for a $3,200 laptop.
prompt: My $3,200 laptop died 8 months after purchase. The manufacturer denied the warranty claim saying it's accidental damage, but it just stopped turning on — I never dropped it. What's my escalation path: retailer, credit card purchase protection, state AG? Give me the order and what to say.

depth_note: Tests third-party home-warranty fine-print analysis for a denied $6,000 HVAC claim.
prompt: My home warranty company denied a $6,000 HVAC replacement, calling it a pre-existing condition. I've had the policy 14 months and the system worked fine until last month. How do I fight the denial — what in the contract actually matters, and when is it worth hiring a lawyer?

depth_note: Tests security-deposit law with penalty multipliers: Illinois 2x damages for bad-faith withholding without itemization.
prompt: My Chicago landlord kept my entire $1,600 security deposit and sent no itemized list within 30 days. The apartment was clean — I have move-out photos. Under Illinois law, what can I recover, and how do I file for the 2x penalty in small claims?

depth_note: Tests negligence vs act-of-God analysis for neighbor property damage and the demand process.
prompt: My neighbor's dead tree fell on my fence during a storm, causing $4,000 in damage. I'd warned him twice in writing that the tree was rotting. His homeowner's insurance denied my claim. Can I sue him in small claims, and does my written warning change the negligence analysis?

depth_note: Tests FDCPA cease-communication rights and debt-validation letter strategy for high-frequency collection calls.
prompt: A collector calls me 5 times a day about a $2,100 old credit card debt, including once at 8:45pm. I asked them to stop calling and they laughed. What are my exact rights, what do I put in a validation letter, and how do I document violations worth $1,000 each?

depth_note: Tests wage-garnishment legality for medical debt and the response steps before a court order exists.
prompt: A collector told me they're going to garnish my wages next week over a $5,400 medical debt. They haven't sued me. Can they actually do that? What's the real legal process for garnishment in Illinois, and what should I do right now?

depth_note: Tests specific FDCPA third-party disclosure violations and the CFPB/state-AG complaint process.
prompt: A debt collector called my boss and told him I owe $3,800 and need to pay immediately. My boss is furious. Which specific FDCPA rules did they break, where do I file complaints, and can I sue them myself?

depth_note: Tests time-barred debt validation strategy: what to request, what never to say, and how to respond to a lawsuit threat.
prompt: A collector is demanding $900 on a credit card debt from 2018. Illinois has a 5-year statute of limitations. How do I get them to validate it without accidentally restarting the clock, and what do I do if they sue me anyway?

depth_note: Tests Chapter 7 vs 13 selection using the means test, home equity exemptions, and income facts.
prompt: I have $60k in credit card debt, earn $45k a year, and own a $200k home with $40k in equity. Should I file Chapter 7 or Chapter 13? Walk me through the means test and whether I'd lose the house.

depth_note: Tests bankruptcy-attorney selection criteria: flat-fee comparison and the questions that reveal competence.
prompt: Two bankruptcy attorneys quoted me $1,800 and $2,500 flat fee for a Chapter 7. What questions do I ask to tell them apart, what should be included in the flat fee versus billed extra, and what are red flags that an attorney will botch my case?

depth_note: Tests Chicago RLTO remedies for uninhabitable conditions: repair-and-deduct vs rent escrow in winter.
prompt: It's January in Chicago, my heat has been out for 6 days, and my landlord won't return calls. Rent is $1,450. Under the Chicago RLTO, can I hire my own repair and deduct it, withhold rent into escrow, or break the lease? Give me the exact steps.

depth_note: Tests retaliation analysis: documenting the timeline when a landlord issues notice after a complaint.
prompt: I filed a 311 complaint about mold in my apartment last month. Yesterday my landlord gave me a 30-day termination notice even though my lease runs 7 more months. Is this retaliation under Illinois law, what evidence do I need, and can he actually force me out?

depth_note: Tests non-compete and signing-bonus clawback risk quantification in a job offer.
prompt: I got a job offer for $130k with a $15k signing bonus, but the contract has a 12-month non-compete covering my entire industry and says I repay the bonus if I leave within 2 years. How do I quantify what these clauses actually cost me, and what should I negotiate?

depth_note: Tests severance evaluation: weighing weeks of pay against a general release of claims after a layoff.
prompt: I was just laid off and they offered 8 weeks of severance — about $18k — but only if I sign a release waiving all legal claims. I think my termination might have been discriminatory. How do I evaluate whether to sign, negotiate for more, or talk to a lawyer first?

depth_note: Tests hidden opportunity cost of NDAs in freelance contracts: quantifying lost portfolio value.
prompt: A client wants me to sign an NDA for a freelance project that would ban me from showing any of the work in my portfolio for 3 years. Portfolio pieces are how I get roughly $30k a year in new business. How do I price that restriction into my fee, or negotiate a carve-out?

depth_note: Tests when NDAs protect versus cost you: mutual NDA before an investor pitch for a startup.
prompt: An investor wants me to sign THEIR mutual NDA before I pitch my startup. I've heard signing investor NDAs is a red flag. When does an NDA actually protect a founder, when does it signal a bad investor, and what should I do here?

depth_note: Tests federal trademark cost-benefit analysis for a small Etsy brand: TEAS Plus vs Standard and whether filing is worth it.
prompt: My Etsy shop makes about $8k a year and the brand name is starting to get copied. Should I file a federal trademark? Compare the $250 TEAS Plus vs $350 standard filing, total real cost with attorney help, and whether it's worth it at my revenue level.

depth_note: Tests common-law enforcement options without a registration: cease-and-desist strategy and evidence of first use.
prompt: Someone started selling under my brand name on Amazon. I never registered a trademark but I've used the name for 3 years and have dated invoices and a website. What can I actually do without a federal registration — cease and desist, Amazon brand registry, or am I out of luck?
